To me, it was quite clear that Dario Kordic was the leading political figure in Central Bosnia for the Croats, but, of course, he did have military responsibilities as well. But, as I say, the political side and the military side were extremely closely interlinked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You will be asked some further questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good afternoon, Sir Martin. My name is Steven Sayers, I am one of the attorneys representing Dario Kordic, and I'll be asking you some questions during the afternoon. Behind me, the attorneys representing the second accused, Mario Cerkez, who is sitting over there to the left. I don't know whether they will have any questions for you. I rather doubt it. Just a few matters of detail to begin with. And to let you know where I am going, I intend to ask some general questions about the institutions that you've identified and whose functions you've described, the personalities that you've mentioned during your direct examination, and then I'll try to take up chronologically, pretty much as the Prosecution has done, and I'll follow on with the meetings that you had with Mr. Kordic, and the other significant events that you've described in your direct examination. Of course, if I ask any questions which are unclear, please let me know. That's my fault, not any lack of understanding on your part, I assure you. Just generally, sir. My understanding is that you were the head of the coordinating centre in Mostar, and that you held that position from June of 1993 until the end of -- approximately the end of September of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is right. When I arrived out in Bosnia, I was sent straight to Mostar and spent my first three months in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that straddled, if you like, the last days of the so-called Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, the HZ-HB, and the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna on the 28th of August of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you became the head of the regional centre of the European Community Monitor Mission in Zenica, taking up your position from your predecessor, Jean-Pierre Thebault, I believe on October the 14th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it's just worth adding that the area of which I was responsible covered all the Croat and Bosniak areas of Bosnia; in other words -- Croat and Bosniak areas; in other words, the new area of the federation, except for Sarajevo, Bihac, and the three pockets of Zepa, Gorazde and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've just described what your area of responsibility was as HRC or the head of the regional centre in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had only been in the area fulfilling your new duties, as the head of the regional centre, for nine days at the time of the Stupni Do incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you yourself speak Croatian, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I am a self-taught speaker. Therefore, I am not very professional. But I do understand a lot, but I speak rather slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you relied upon the services of interpreters to conduct the exchanges that you had --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- with various people? Very well. I was going to ask you some general questions regarding the make-up of the European Community Monitoring Mission, but the Trial Chamber's heard more than sufficient evidence on that, so let me pass on to the next question. The general military situation that confronted you, as you assumed your duties as head of the regional centre in Zenica, it would be fair to say that militarily, at least, the Croats were very much on the defensive throughout your time as HRC Zenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is largely so. If I could just, perhaps just to help the Court -- the three areas of my -- three areas for which I was responsible were very different. Tuzla, the Bosniaks and the Croats were fighting together against the Serbs. In Central Bosnia, the Croats and the Bosniaks were fighting between themselves. And in the southern part, the main fighting was going on in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree, sir, that this was a fairly complex kaleidoscopic patchwork quilt of shifting alliances and political orientations, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can summarise the situation that the Croats found themselves in, at least from your perspective, when you assumed your duties, sir. Would it be fair to say that by the middle of November of 1993, after you had been in the job for some time, the Croats had essentially been squeezed or compressed into three geographically, politically and militarily isolated pockets: the Vitez-Busovaca pocket, the Kiseljak pocket, and the town of Zepce?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Vares pocket had essentially disappeared as a result of the ABiH onslaught in the very early part of November?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made some reference during your direct examination to a conversation that you had with Mate Boban, one of the subjects of which was the departure of 12.000 or so Croats from Kakanj. You mentioned that you were not particularly familiar with the facts surrounding that, but would it be -- would it help jog your memory to suggest that there was an offensive launched by Muslim forces on the town of Kakanj from June the 9th to the 13th of 1993, and that that was what resulted in this huge exodus of refugees?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I would agree. I would agree. But inevitably, because I was so bound up with Mostar at that time, I was not paying detailed attention to Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, of course not, Sir Martin. That was someone else's bailiwick, and it didn't become your bailiwick until October of 1993.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And isn't it true that one of the leaders of the gangs that were controlled by Ivica Rajic, one of the subcommanders, if you like, a gentleman by the name of Dzeljo [phoen], and I believe he is referred to in your November 3rd report, this gentleman what was actually a emigre from Kakanj, having been ejected along with the 12.000 or so refugees in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That could well be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall that the leader of this gang of persons nicknamed the Apostoli, that his parents had actually been killed in Bilalovac by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I knew that. I don't think I knew that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, sir, that the political and the military components of the warring forces were, I think you used the words, inextricably intertwined. Who was the political commander on the Muslim side in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, in fact, in Central Bosnia my main dealings were on the military side. In fact, I used to talk politics to the Bosnian commanders. I did not have so much dealing -- Mirsad Ceman was President of the SDA in the area and I had one or two meetings with him, but the main authority or the main driving force on the Bosniak side was the military side, or those were my main interlocutors for trying to achieve results.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't aware of Mr. Ceman having any military functions, military powers, the ability to issue orders to the Armija forces, were you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I never saw him at any meeting involving the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just giving the interpreters a chance to catch up. Your principal dealings, I believe, with the leaders of the Muslim forces were, first, with General Enver Hadzihasanovic and subsequently with General Mehmet Alagic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You found both of these gentlemen to be hard-liners, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, generally you found all of the Muslim military leadership to fall into that category of being hard-liners, in your view; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, they were very single-minded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, I believe that you reflected that on page 2 of your end-of-tour report, which has previously been marked Exhibit D19/1 and, I think, Exhibit Z1419 by the Prosecution this morning.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just add that Hadzihasanovic came from Zvornik and Alagic came from Sanski Most, and they both told me several times that they would not stop fighting until they were back living in the places where they were born.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or until they had subsequently resumed possession, militarily, of all of the properties that once they, at least in their view, controlled before the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, but they specifically said that they -- you know, Hadzihasanovic in Zvornik, Alagic in Sanski Most, but they were determined to fight on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, it was your view that the Muslim generals had learned their lessons very well from the Serbs and that, possession being nine-tenths of the law at the negotiation table, that's exactly the policy that they were pursuing; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: It was certainly my view that the lesson was not lost at all, that the Serbs had actually demonstrated that territorial possession was nine-tenths of the law when it came to the negotiation table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I'll just ask you some questions in connection with the Kakanj offensive from June the 9th to the 13th. Perhaps you don't have any individual knowledge of this, but isn't it also true that there was a simultaneous offensive going on in the Travnik area from June the 8th to the 12th of 1993, and that actually produced, we heard a witness testify a few days ago, about 20.000 refugees, Croat refugees?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, this is so, but I regret I'm not in a position to give detailed answers on those two campaigns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I won't ask you any. It's also true, is it not, that a simultaneous -- actually, not a simultaneous but a subsequent military offensive was launched in Bugojno and in Fojnica, both of those municipalities were captured by Muslim forces, and they also resulted in tens of thousands of Bosnian Croat refugees as well?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from the Vares offensive that resulted in the capture of Vares, there were two other offensives that occurred during your tour of duty. I think they are referred to on page 2 of your end-of-tour report, Sir Martin, and feel free to consult it, if you need. But I believe that the first was on December 22nd, just before Christmas of 1993, before a major attack was launched by [realtime transcript read in error "on"] the Muslim forces on the Vitez-Busovaca pocket. You were familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That produced many Croat fatalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see that the transcript says "launched on the Muslims," but it's actually "launched by the Muslim forces"; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Sorry, can I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at line 4 on page 66. The transcript reads, "A military offensive was launched on the Muslims," but it actually should read, "A military offensive was launched by the Muslim --"

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: On page --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, on the screen before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can see that that's wrong. There's no need to trouble with that.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Sorry, a major offensive was launched -- line 4 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should read "by the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what this page 66 is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't worry, Sir Martin. Counsel is confusing the issue by referring to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Right, okay. Well, the major offensive just before Christmas was, of course, launched by the Muslims on the Vitez pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that cleans up the transcript, Mr. President. Sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the second offensive, Sir Martin, I take it was in the second week of January, January the 9th, to be precise, when a major offensive was launched on the Vitez-Busovaca pocket at Santici, aimed at controlling the main supply route at that location?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were you aware that house-to-house clearance techniques were used in these offensives that resulted in the deaths of many Croat civilians?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let me stand aside and just ask you, sir, you've made considerable reference to the HVO during your testimony. It's true, is it not, that throughout the period August of 1992 until the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, the President of the HVO was Dr. Jadranko Prlic in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall any discussions with influential Croats in Mostar, such as, for example, Vladislav Pogarcic, regarding the intention behind setting up the HVO, whether it was permanent, whether it was temporary, or temporary expedient in wartime; do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I had discussions with Vladislav Pogarcic on a number of occasions, but we certainly never discussed the reason for the establishment of the HVO, which I think by its title was, to me, sort of self-evident. It was their defence council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Defence against the Serbs, who had launched massive offensives throughout the territory of the new Republic which was only founded, I believe, on March the 6th of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, did you ever undertake any effort to ascertain for yourself what the powers of a President of the HVO were?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Not specifically, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me move on to the next subject. I'll suggest to you, and I don't believe that this is controverted, that there were three Vice-Presidents of the HVO, the first being a man called Stipo Ivankovic, who was appointed to his position simultaneously with the appointment of Dr. Prlic as President. Did you ever see Mr. Ivankovic?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I don't think I ever met Mr. Ivankovic, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The Second Vice-President is Anto Valenta, and he was appointed, I believe, on October the 17th, 1992. You did meet him?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he described to you the fact that he was, in fact, a Vice-President of the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. No, wait a minute. I would have to check on that. I think it is likely, but I cannot recall Valenta actually saying to me, "I'm a Vice-President of the HVO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The Third Vice-President, sir, is a gentleman that you mentioned by the name of Kresimir Zubak. Did you meet him in Mostar before the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that he was a Vice-President of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In fact, I think I mentioned that in my evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that, in fact, Mr. Kordic was never a Vice-President of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, I certainly was convinced that he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me put it to you that the only official position that he held in the HVO was as one of many members of a personnel committee, to which he was appointed in 1992, in November, I believe.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: As far as the HVO is concerned?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I was not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same question with respect to the powers of a President: Did you ever take any steps to inform yourself or to investigate what the powers of a Vice-President of the HVO may have been, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I did not go into the terms of reference, no, of Prlic, Zubak and the others, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Turning to the political party, the HDZ-BiH, you were aware, I think, that Mr. Mate Boban was the President of this political party at all material times --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that are involved in this case, and I believe that you have identified Mr. Kordic correctly as one of the Vice-Presidents of the political party. Do you know how many Vice-Presidents there were?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just have one document marked as an exhibit. I would like to ask you if you've ever seen a copy of this before and if you are aware of the other Vice-Presidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't see any point in this. The witness has said that he was not aware and he doesn't know how many Vice-Presidents there were, so there's no point asking him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that may be correct. Let me just put the proposition to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the proposition? What is it, before you put it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That there were five Vice-Presidents appointed in November of 1992, and Mr. Kordic was one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Sir Martin, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: If I guessed, I would have said approximately six, but I did not know it was precisely five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, you can call evidence about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mr. Mile Akmadzic, one of the other Vice-Presidents?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I did not know Akmadzic, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the other Vice-Presidents was Pero Markovic. I believe you may have met him.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly met Markovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jadranko Topic?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You met him too; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Ivo Zivkovic?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Zivkovic, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Sir Martin, in connection with the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna in August of 1993, you were aware, I take it, of the progress of the international negotiations starting first with the internationally-sanctioned and approved Vance-Owen Plan, or so-called Vance-Owen Plan, in early 1993 and progressing on to the Stoltenberg-Owen Plan --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the final incarnation of which was approved, I believe, in August of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the foundation of that plan -- and the Trial Chamber has heard evidence of this already, but it may be useful to go over this -- the foundation of the plan was the establishment of three ethnically-based constituent or so-called constituent republics which would collectively form the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand the position of the International Community, it was anticipated that each one of these republics would be self-governing, with elected representatives, and in turn there would be superimposed upon the constituent republic structure a central government to which each of the three republics would appoint various representatives?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. In general terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You were aware, sir, that Dr. Prlic was appointed to be the Prime Minister of the Government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that there were a number of ministers appointed simultaneously with him?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kordic was not one of those ministers, was he?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that there were two Deputy Prime Ministers subordinate to Dr. Prlic, the first being Perica Jukic from Zepce and the second being Jozo Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Now that you say it, it does ring a bell, but I would not have been able to remember it off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I take it that you are aware that Mr. Boban was the hold-over President from the HZ-HB. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he fulfilled that role until, I think you've said, approximately the middle of February of 1994?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You also made reference to a Presidential Council, sir, that I believe was appointed on the 10th of December. Were you aware of the people who were appointed on this council?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I cannot recall, but I'm aware that Dario Kordic was appointed at some stage. I'm not quite sure on what date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put it to you, sir, that Mr. Kordic was not appointed to this council until October of 1994, well after the close of the war.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Right, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that appointed to the council on December the 10th, 1993, were Lieutenant-General Ante Roso, who was the Commander In Chief of the HVO Armed Forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the gentlemen that you previously described, sir, Ivo Lozancic, who was President of the HVO in Zepce; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that those two gentlemen were on the Presidential Council?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Now that you remind me, probably, yes. But, again, I wouldn't have had it on the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true, is it not, that Mr. Kordic was never on the Presidential Council during any time when you were HRC Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I knew he came onto the council, but I was not sure -- I could not identify when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, just turning to the government, sir, were you aware that the Government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna consisted of a President and a House of Representatives, a Parliament, if you like?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I take it that you were aware that the first convention of the House of Representatives was held on November the 20th, 1993, and I believe you've been asked some questions in connection with Mr. Boban's press advisor, Slobodan Lovrinovic, --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- with whom the ECMM had a fairly continuous relationship; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: A fairly regular relationship, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe it was on November the 20th that you identified that General Roso was known by the ECMM to have replaced General Praljak as the new Commander In Chief of the HVO Armed Forces throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. I would have to check the precise date, but it was about -- in fact, I think it was a week after the destruction of the Stari mosque, which must have been the 16th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question regarding General Praljak. Did you know that he was actually born in Capljina in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have previously described conversations you had with the head of the coordination centre in Mostar, sir, Mr. Philip Watkins. He had actually attended the parliamentary session of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna on February the 17th of 1994, and I think you've described --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that you found out from him, as a result of his attendance at that session, that Ivan Bender had actually been elected the President at the Parliament.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I think you said, sir, that your impression was that Mr. Kordic had been elected Vice-President of the parliament and that he was one of three such Vice-Presidents.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or Deputy Chairmen, actually.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware that actually there were only two Deputy Chairmen, Mr. Kordic of course being one of them, and Vlado Santic of Bihac being the second one?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I must say I thought -- I was under the impression he was one of three Vice-Presidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If I could just ask for this document to be marked as an exhibit. Have one put on the ELMO. I only have one question for you in connection with it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D174/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, this is a translation of a document published in the Narodni List in March of 1994. Did your monitors actually have access to the Narodni List?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Probably. Probably, but I couldn't say for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Looking at this document, sir, and since you apparently read Croatian, feel free to look at the Croatian original that's attached to this. Does this help refresh your recollection, that Mr. Kordic and Mr. Santic were appointed as Deputy Chairmen of the Chamber Of Deputies by the Chairman of that Chamber, Ivan Bender?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. But again I do not recall seeing this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with the document. I appreciate it. You made reference to President Boban's resignation in February of 1994. Isn't it true that the general feeling among Croats was that he had resigned for entirely honourable reasons?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I think the reaction was somewhat mute amongst the Croats. I expected a more strong reaction. And I think all the Croats accepted his resignation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I just refer you to page 15 of the statement that you gave in February 1998. I don't think you are saying anything different. You say that: "At about this time Mate Boban resigned from his post as President of the CRHB. Reaction to this resignation amongst the Croats in Central Bosnia was surprisingly mute. The general feeling seemed to be that he resigned for honourable reasons, as he had other important work to do." And that's still your view today --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is it not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Perhaps I could just add a rider to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I mean, I do not know. I do not know. I mean, one heard, although I cannot prove it, that pressure was put on Franjo Tudjman, over the peace negotiations, that Mate Boban should go. I cannot say whether that is true or not. So all I can say is that the Croat reaction to his departure was mute, surprisingly mute. The precise reasons why he went, I could not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let me move on to one other connected subject. You were aware, from reports that you had received from your associates in Mostar, that in fact there was no position of Vice-President in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, as I say, I had assumed -- my understanding was that Dario Kordic had been appointed to the Vice-President, but it could be that I was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if I might just ask you, Sir Martin, to take a look at the document that was marked Exhibit Z13310. I believe that's already been marked as an exhibit. We may have to present that to Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Right. I don't think I've got it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I wonder if, Mr. Usher, you can just put this on the ELMO, please, another copy of it. Page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a confidential document; the Registrar says so. It can't go on the ELMO. What is the point, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: A very simple point, Mr. President. Mr. Lovrenovic informs the ECMM that the Presidential Council was formed because the CRHB or the HRHB has no Vice-Presidents, and the Presidential Council is formed as an alternative mechanism that was needed to support the Presidential Office in President Boban's absence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that help jog your memory, Sir Martin?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In fact, I think -- in fact, I think I said that in my statement, in fact, because I actually quoted the statement by Lovrenovic about extracting someone who was aware here from Central Bosnia would sent the wrong message. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. And I believe, sir, that you were aware that your HCC in Mostar had been informed, on a number of occasions, that actually, when the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was formed, and before his appointment as Deputy Chairman of the House of Representatives, Mr. Kordic was actually just one of a number of ordinary members of the House of Representatives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, I would say more equal than others. I am still convinced, and I was throughout, that Dario Kordic's position was very significant in the hierarchy of the Croats, regardless of what position he might have held at one stage or at another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. The question was, though, that your representatives were actually informed in Mostar that Mr. Kordic was just an ordinary member of the House of Representatives; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, while we are dealing with these matters, the witness's evidence is that in the HVO the civil and military sides were, as he put it, intertwined, and that he would deal with military leaders about political matters, and political leaders about military matters. Now, we've had evidence much to this effect before, and I don't remember it being challenged. I may be wrong. And it would help us to know what your case is about this. Is it accepted that there was such an intertwining, as it's put, between civil and military matters, or is that disputed?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That proposition is in fact disputed, Mr. President. Our position is that Mr. Kordic was a significant political leader in Central Bosnia. Indeed, I think the evidence on that is absolutely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need to argue the point. It's just we want to know what your position is. Your position is that he was a significant political leader. You said that before. The question is: Is it accepted that civil and military matters were in the HVO intertwined, as the witness's evidence is?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The answer to the question, Your Honour, insofar as Sir Martin's testimony is concerned, the time period covered by his testimony is that is not accepted. In the extremely early days of the HVO, when it was originally formed, by decree of Mate Boban on the 8th of April 1992, I think it would be correct to say that there was a significant degree of intermixture between civilian and military functions inside the HVO, because the entity, the organisation, was evolving, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with that. Formed in April 1992. How long is it accepted that there was such an intertwining?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's extremely difficult to say, but I would -- if you are seeking my views --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not your views. It's your case, you see. What are you going to say to us at the end of this trial about this sort of evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think our case is, Your Honour, that the intermingling of functions continued until the military organisation of the HVO was actually established. And that would have been around, I think, July, August of 1992, when Colonel Blaskic was appointed to the position of head of the Central -- or commander of the Central Bosnia operative zone, as it was then known, and it became the third operative zone of the HVO, I believe, when Sir Martin was fulfilling his functions as HRC Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And your case, then, is that thereafter there was not an intertwining of the civil and military?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't know what "intertwining" means, Your Honour, but our position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a perfectly straightforward English word.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Our position is, Your Honour, and I think that this has been our position throughout this entire case, that there was a separate chain of command in the military; that Colonel Blaskic reported directly in the chain of command to his Superior Officer, who was the Chief in Mostar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. You should give the witness the opportunity of dealing with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I intend to do that. I intend to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, this would appear to be as good a time as any to address that subject, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, isn't it true that the headquarters of the general staff of the HVO, as a military organisation, was actually located in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Commander In Chief, during your tenure as HRC Zenica, was initially, as you've said, General Slobodan Praljak, followed by Lieutenant-General Ante Roso?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A soldier's soldier, I think you described him. And isn't it true that the military organisation of the HVO was that beneath the general staff, the military forces were organised into various so-called operative zones, each commanded by a separate individual. In Central Bosnia, for example, Commander Blaskic, him being the commander of the Central Bosnia operative zone, or the third operation zone, as it was later known. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Indeed, absolutely. But of course with extremely close political control throughout. And in my view, it was the political side which was actually controlling events on the ground, as it should be. As it should be. Because, of course, the military are answerable to the politicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. Colonel Blaskic never once intimated to you, or any of your monitors, as far as you are aware, that he had to take orders from Mr. Kordic, did he?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military orders. In fact, there are no reports whatsoever, within the body of the European Community Monitoring Mission, at the most basic monitor level, to the CC level, and the RC level, or in reports sent to the Head Of Mission in Zagreb, that make that contention, are there?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No. Of course, there is a military chain of command, but that military chain of command is overshadowed by the political control. And that is what I always was convinced was the case in Bosnia, and that would not surprise me at all, because that's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. But in the chain of command --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Commanding Officer, as you would expect in any military organisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, you are being asked to slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that, as you would expect in any organisation, hierarchically, Colonel Blaskic reported directly to his Commanding Officer, who was the Chief Of The General Staff in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I'm sure he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, proceeding down the chain, if you like. And perhaps this is beneath the level of detail with which you became acquainted. If it is, just tell me. Isn't it true that within each operative zone, the military organisation was in municipality-based brigades, each commanded by a separate Commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. But I must stress once again that at any stage the political side can overrule the military, as again is quite correct; at any stage in that chain. The military are in support of the politicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you yourself did not have any discussions with President Boban or Dr. Prlic, or any other politicians, as far as you can remember, concerning the actual military chain of command, the way in which orders were given and carried out?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I did not discuss that with President Boban, or Mr. Boban, or any other political leaders, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Let me just ask one other question. You never actually saw Mr. Boban and Mr. Kordic in each other's company, did you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you've discussed the alleged family relationship between Mr. Kordic and Mr. Boban. I would just like to suggest to you that, in fact, there was no relationship; that just represented the popular wisdom that filtered down to you and others during your tour of duty. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's right. As I said, I had no proof. It was just an understanding that I had for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few questions in connection with the extent -- of the geographical extent, if you like, Sir Martin, of Mr. Kordic's political influence. You are not suggesting that his political influence extended all the way down to Mostar, are you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No. I believe his political influence really covered the areas -- well, as I say, Tuzla, Central Bosnia and then Herzegovina. And I believe his political influence was Central Bosnia, from the border with Tuzla, down to the borders of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you would agree that he had no discernible, political power influence in Mostar, so far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Except for his very considerable stature in Central Bosnia, I would say that he probably had a lot of say in what went on in Mostar, yes. I would have been surprised if that was not so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he never took any part in the Government of Mostar, so far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never saw him in Mostar at any time during your tour of duty in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: When I was in Zenica, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just a few questions on personalities. I think you've already described President Boban sufficiently. Let's go on to Dr. Prlic. In your view, he was the most impressive of all of the Bosnian Croat politicians that you met; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's what I wrote in my report, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Insofar as Mr. Zubak is concerned, I believe that he was the representative of the Government of the Croatian Republic who actually signed the Washington Agreements that terminated the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct. The Dayton Agreement was signed by Prlic, not Zubak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a year later --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: A year later, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked several questions concerning comments made by Mr. Kordic regarding his views on the progress of Islamic fundamentalism in the Government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the fears that he expressed in that regard. Wouldn't it be fair to say, sir, that this was a constant theme that was repeated to you by virtually all Croat leaders up to this very day?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And indeed some of them, including the late President Franjo Tudjman, were very paranoid about Islamic fundamentalism. I used to raise this with the -- particularly with the Generals. I am particularly thinking Hadzihasanovic and Alagic, who, more often than not, were sitting there drinking a glass or two of slivovitz and not looking at all like fundamentalists to me. And they both used to laugh me out of Court, and said that, you know, they were absolutely 100 per cent against fundamentalism. But this was a constant theme from the Croats, and indeed from the Roman Catholic Church. It was put to me on a number of occasions. So it was a strong feeling, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be equally fair to say that there was nothing particularly significant or eccentric about the views that were being expressed to you by Mr. Kordic, those being views that were familially expressed by representatives of the Croat Government with whom you regularly --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: The views on Islamic fundamentalism were common to, I would say, the majority of Croat leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, you described four or five meetings that you had with Mr. Kordic, as far as you could remember, although it may have been more. You've stated that you never asked Mr. Kordic if he held any military rank, but you also never enquired whether he had any power or authority to issue military orders, specifically, did you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I did not ask that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never actually saw or heard him do that, issue military orders, did you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I never heard him give a military order, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And you were never told by any Bosnian Croat military commander that he did in fact have that power or authority, were you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. All right. The next subject that I have on my note says Mr. Kordic's positions, but I think we've covered that perfectly well. At this point, Sir Martin, I'd like to progress chronologically with you, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers. I'm sorry, we were conferring.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I was going to proceed chronologically with Sir Martin over the meetings and events that he's discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That would be a convenient moment to adjourn. We'll adjourn now till half past 2.00. Sir Martin, I must tell you, as I tell all witnesses, don't speak to anybody, please, about your evidence until it's over. And don't let anybody speak to you about it. And that does include members of the Prosecution. Could you be back, please, at half past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m. 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first event chronologically about which you testified was a meeting or two meetings that you had on October the 21st, 1993, one with Mr. Valenta and one with Mr. Kordic. It would be fair to say, sir, that you were accompanied on this meeting by your V-1 monitor, Nick Turnbull; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Certainly to the meeting with Dario Kordic, I'm not sure whether he was -- yes -- no, it was HCC Travnik that was with me when I met Anto Valenta, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would have been Mr. Watkins at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Mr. Watkins at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Turnbull was the V-1 monitor specifically assigned to be responsible for the Vitez-Busovaca area, amongst others; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at this time when you had been, for less than a week, essentially, in your new position, he would have been the person most familiar with the military and political situation in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No. Watkins was the one who had been there longest. He had been there for nearly a year, and he was the one who was most familiar with the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You testified that you visited Mr. Kordic at a house outside of Busovaca referred to as the Eagle's Nest. Whose nickname was that for this?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I believe it was the nickname -- I don't think -- I'm not sure whether it was called Eagle's Nest by the Croats, but it was certainly the name given it by the International Community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know that the Bobovac Brigade headquarters was also referred to as the Eagle's Nest by the International Community, specifically by NordBat?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I certainly never heard it referred to as Eagle's Nest, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that Mr. Kordic expressed various views on the likelihood of Croats returning to Zenica at the conclusion of hostilities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Zenica at this time, sir, was a Muslim-controlled city; it was controlled completely by armed forces under the Armija. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware, were you, sir, that the HVO armed forces in that city had been defeated during the April fighting and that the two HVO brigades located in that city had been eliminated?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the position was, as I take it, that Croats would not necessarily return to the houses from which they had left because, A, they had left of their own free will and, B, they might not feel protected moving back to a city that was not under the control of HVO or Croat forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. There were a large number of Croats still in Zenica, but of course very much fewer than there had been before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's no question that those views expressed by Mr. Kordic were perfectly reasonable under the circumstances, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, those were his views, and he said that he thought it was unlikely that many of them would remain unless they were being properly treated by the Serbs and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked by the investigators for the Prosecution specifically whether these comments indicated to you that Mr. Kordic advocated some sort of permanent division of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina along ethnic lines; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your response was that there was nothing about these comments that would indicate to you that Mr. Kordic in any way wished to see a division of the three ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I think I said what I -- I think I actually said -- I haven't got my words in front of me -- was that I did not think the words, in themselves, indicated a wish to see three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. On page 6 of the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor's investigators two years ago, you said, in response to the question of whether these views expressed by Mr. Kordic would advocate a permanent division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you said: "My reply is that I could not say the words used by Dario Kordic, as such, indicated that he wished to see a division of the three ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct. I hope that's what I've just said; I hope so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that remained the case throughout your tour as HRC Zenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were also shown a copy of the daily report, sir, that RC Zenica submitted on October the 21st. That was Z1255. Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was at this meeting that you were -- you said on page 2 that Mr. -- you had a meeting with Mr. Dario Kordic, Vice-President, HZ Middle Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you described him as one of the two most influential Croat civil leaders in Central Bosnia on page 6?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me address your attention, Sir Martin, to the Stupni Do incident. I am finished with that document. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'd like to go fairly carefully through these events. The first thing that I would like to address is events before Stupni Do; the second is issues related to ECMM reports regarding the black market thriving there, apparently; and the third is the investigations that were done by NordBat and others after the incident. Turning to the first subject. Stupni Do is located on a hillside in a small valley that overlooks the main supply route directly into the town of Vares; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to give the Trial Chamber some sense of Vares's physical location, it really stands at the head of a valley, does it not?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With tall hills and mountains all around the city, and, essentially, the only way into it, and out of it, is the main supply route right past Stupni Do; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some testimony, sir, regarding events at a village called Kopjari. Were you aware that this village had been attacked by Muslim forces on the 22nd of October, 1993, at about 5.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I was aware there had been an attack, but I also was convinced, and still am, that nothing serious had taken place there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know that, according to NordBat anyway, heavy fighting had been going on in that city, and all of the civilians had been expelled from the -- not the city; from the village, and that all of the civilians had been expelled from the village by Armija forces?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I am aware that there had been incidents in Kopjari, but I am not aware of any deaths. And of course we did have somewhat more serious matters to deal with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that all of the houses and buildings in Kopjari had been burned down and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I'm aware that there had been destruction, but, by the scale of events compared with Stupni Do, this was comparatively minor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just show you a daily report that was prepared from the regional centre of Zenica on March the 21st of 1994, which, by the way, Sir Martin, was still within your tour of duty; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: March the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: March the 21st, 1994, sir.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I might -- I was sent back to England on medical grounds towards the end of March, and I'm not quite sure when I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D175/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd just like to draw your attention, sir -- even though it is not numbered, this is something that we have received from the Prosecution. It appears to be the fourth page in under the subheading "Humanitarian." Put that on the ELMO, please. Thank you. If you can see towards the end of the paragraph that says: "ECMM visited Lipnica." The second sentence says: "ECMM also visited Kopjari and noted that all buildings had been destroyed and the village is uninhabited."

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that help jog your memory, Sir Martin --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I do not recall seeing this report. I cannot remember when I returned to England on medical grounds, but it was certainly the end of March, but I do not recall seeing this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm through with that. The next document that I would like you to review, if I may, is an exhibit that has previously been marked Exhibit D123/1, which is a military intelligence summary from the Prince of Wales Own Regiment of Yorkshire, dated October the 27, 1993. And if I could just ask the Registrar to turn to page 2, right up at the top. There is a reference to a conversation that the Commanding Officer of the Prince of Wales Own Regiment, 1st Battalion, had with Colonel Merdan relating to Kopjari. And apparently the impression given by Colonel Merdan was that the attack was a punitive action, and did not press a more general attack on Vares itself. Did you have any discussions with any members of BritBat concerning the attack on Kopjari and its depiction as a punitive action on the attacking forces?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was a punitive action?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I was not aware that it was designed as a punitive action, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you testified on direct examination, sir, that the ECMM checked out Kopjari and, I think to use your words, "nothing significant transpired," does information that all of the building had been destroyed and all of the members of the population had been ejected from the village, does that change your view that nothing significant had transpired?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Certainly, the way you put it, it sounds serious, but of course there were other more serious incidents going on at the time, and the things taken on a matter of priority in these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I fully appreciate that it's a matter of scale. And the fact of the matter is that terrible things were going on on both sides throughout this civil war; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next subject I would like to address with you is the subject of Stupni Do as a black market gateway. I wonder if I could ask you to be shown the next exhibit. I believe it's already been introduced into evidence by the Prosecution, Z1281, which is a daily report of the regional centre in Zenica on November the 2nd, 1993. Thank you. If you could, Mr. Usher, just place the first page under "CC Travnik AOR" on the -- that's it. Yes. Now, sir, this is a document which, of course, you've seen at some point. Did you review this document as you prepared for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, not specifically. Not specifically this document, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just review it with you. Apparently, the head of the coordination centre in Travnik had had a meeting with a Mr. Mahmutovic, who was a member of the Armija operative group in Dabravine. Just for the Trial Chamber's information, Dabravine is actually located a few kilometres south of Vares, on the main supply route; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it not true that Dabravine was the headquarters of the war presidency in exile, headed up by a lady by the name of Mervana Hadjimurtezic?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, according to the head of the coordination centre in Travnik, who I believe was Colonel Stutt at this time, Stupni Do was the local gateway to BSA-controlled territory, and this made it a most lucrative centre for smuggling and black marketing. It's true, is it not, that several ECMM reports relating to black market activity in the region of Stupni Do had been prepared, and reviewed in due course?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. And of course I hinted at this in my end-of-tour report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, we have not been able to locate or been provided with any of those. But this was not a secret, was it? It was a relatively well-known fact that Stupni Do was being located close to the front lines with Bosnian Serb forces; it served as a channel, or funnel, if you like, through which a lot of black market --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: There was certainly allegations that this was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed, according to the Armija member communicating this information to your organisation, sir, those who were killed in Stupni Do were executed deliberately for their part in the black market. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: As I say, I hinted at this -- I alluded to this in my end-of-tour report, saying that this was a possible cause for the attack on Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And, indeed, the information had been communicated to you that shortly before the Stupni Do killings, the local HVO had demanded a higher cut of the black market proceeds and had been given a resounding "no" by the residents of Stupni Do; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: There is an allegation by a member of the BiH OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just turn to page 3 of this document, sir, or page 4, I'm sorry. The document isn't itself numbered, but there's a reference towards the end of this document regarding a discussion of this subject with General Hadzihasanovic. It's just in the first full paragraph, sir. It says: "General Hadzihasanovic told HOM that Vares was known as an area for smugglers, and gangs and groups of smugglers had been sent there to keep up tension." Who was the Head of the Mission to whom General Hadzihasanovic communicated this information, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Can I just have a look at the report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That would be in a meeting with the Head Of Mission, but I can soon check because it will refer to -- no, "HOM" would be-- can only mean Head Of Mssion of the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. The question was: Do you remember, this late removed, who that was?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Well, at this time in November, it was Ambassador de Baans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: But I'm just trying to remember what meeting that was. It must have been the meeting on the 30th of October, where we -- when he came to Zenica and we had meetings with Hadzihasanovic, amongst others. But I can soon check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember being present at that meeting --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, I was certainly present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall now, seeing the document, that General Hadzihasanovic actually confirmed these rumours of black market activity in the Stupni Do area, speaking, as he was, as commander of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. I said in my report that Hadzihasanovic went on to say that gangs and groups of smugglers had been sent to the area to keep the tension high. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am finished with that document too. I appreciate your assistance. Just turning to one of the comments made in the end-of-tour report that you authored, Sir Martin, on the 18th of April, 1994, which is Exhibit Z1419, I believe, your conclusion in paragraph 5 on page 1 --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Sorry. Can I just get hold of it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: One minute. On paragraph --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 on page 1, sir.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that: "It is likely that the decision to mount the operation in Stupni Do was taken at a fairly low level, and it is possible that the massacre was triggered by the refusal of the Muslims in Stupni Do, so the story goes, to pay more to the local HVO from their profits from smuggling operations."

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote at the time, which ties in with the papers we've just been looking at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those, I take it, sir, remain your views today.

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I had -- I still, to this day, do not know who gave the instructions for the massacre in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But nothing has intervened in the last six years or so to persuade you to reach a conclusion different from the one that's reflected in paragraph 5, and that is, to use your words, "It is likely the decision to mount the operation was taken at fairly low level"?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I've had -- no, I've had no information in the intervening years which has added to my knowledge of what triggered the massacre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, or changed your views in any way --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- regarding that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one matter of fairly precise chronological detail. My understanding is that following the news that there had been killings of a lot of civilians and others in Stupni Do, sir, an attempt was made by monitors under your supervision or command -- and we've heard from some of them, Colonel Weckesser being one of them -- an attempt was made to obtain access to Stupni Do, and, as I understand it, following the news of the massacre, that access was actually barred to them by the Bobovac Brigade commander, who at that time was Emil Harah; is that consistent with your --

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: That's correct. Basically, he was stopping, in fact, even Nordbat. The army unit could not get in, and, of course, we could not get in unless the UNPROFOR unit was going in as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Indeed, the point I was getting at, though, was that the access to the village was actually barred on orders of Emil Harah, who was still the Bobovac Brigade leader at that point?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And following that incident, we know from your testimony, and I think it's not controverted, that Mr. Harah was apparently dismissed from his position as Bobovac Brigade commander, to be replaced by Kresimir Bozic, as you've testified; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware, sir, that two days before the fighting at Stupni Do, the civilians, the civilian population of the village, had been ordered to evacuate the village by Mervana Hadjimurtezic, who was the President of the War Presidency in exile in Dabravine?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: No, I don't think I was aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. I wonder if I could ask the usher to show you the next document. It's a report of the Secretary-General of the U.N. about Stupni Do. I believe it's report S/1994/154, dated February the 10th, 1994, and marked Exhibit D118/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I can't remember this document offhand. Is that going to refer to the order for evacuation of the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the witness has said that he didn't remember that. There's no point going over it again. You can make the point to us in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Actually, if I may, Mr. President, there are several points that are raised during the historical recitation contained in that document. I'm happy to tell you exactly what they are. First, it says that the residents of Stupni Do were warned to leave on October the 22nd; and, second, that there were 36 soldiers in the village; third, that there was an investigation performed by apparently UNPROFOR representatives and that there were 193 survivors, all of whom were interviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sir Martin, did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: I wouldn't dispute -- I wouldn't dispute that, no. I would not have been able to say how many survivors there were, but I'm prepared to accept those figures, if that's in that U.N. report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I think, just for the Trial Chamber's own reference, Exhibit D118/1 is a fairly short document. It says that precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you referred earlier, sir, to two orders that had apparently been issued by General Petkovic, and I think that they were appended to ECMM reports. Let me see if I can jog your memory as to what they were. I have copies of both of them, I believe. One has already been marked, I believe, as Exhibit Z1258, and the second one, which is dated October the 24th, 1993, needs a new exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is marked D176/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I wonder if Sir Martin could also be given a copy of Exhibit Z1258, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, just drawing your attention chronologically to the first of these documents, Exhibit Z1258 appears to be a copy of an order issued by General Milivoj Petkovic on the 23rd of October, 1993, and issued to his subordinate, the HVO Vares commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this authorises the commander of the HVO forces in Vares to remove three people from their functions, the first being Anto Pejinovic; the second being Zvonko Duznovic; and the third being Ivica Gavran?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition, he says, to the HVO commander, that: He must investigate the responsibility for the situation in Croatian and Muslim villages where, in accordance with our incomplete findings, ethnic cleansing of the population occurred. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the Trial Chamber's information, Mr. Pejinovic, I believe, was the HVO President of Vares municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Duznovic, apparently, was the Chief Of Military Police in that town?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Gavran was the Chief Of Civilian Police, I believe?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Correct, yes. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second document, Sir Martin, is another order entered or issued to the Commander of the Bobovac Brigade by General Petkovic, one day later, on October the 24th, 1993, ordering the cessation of all combat activities against UNPROFOR members immediately, and ordering unhindered passage for all vehicles; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other things that it refers to, obviously. All right. Thank you. I am finished with those documents. Obviously, Sir Martin, it goes without saying that General Petkovic, the Chief Of Staff of the HVO, had the capability of issuing such military orders to his subordinates, amongst whom were counted the commanders of the HVO in Vares; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. He also, evidently, had the power to remove civilian members of government from the government, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SIR MARTIN GARROD
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly in those particular circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Turning our attention away from those orders for one second.
